items.title: Suspected cyberattack disables supermarket fridges in Belgium and Ireland
items.why: Refrigeration systems failed overnight into Monday at more than 40 Delhaize stores and about 15 Carrefour stores in Belgium, VRT and Euronews report, in what Delhaize calls an 'IT incident'. In Ireland, SuperValu's owner Musgrave said a suspected cyber attack hit fridges in 13 stores.
items.matters: It follows a similar attack on refrigeration systems at hundreds of French supermarkets in October that forced stores to throw away food.

items.title: Ryanair's half-year profit falls 15% as Iran war lifts fuel costs
items.why: Europe's biggest budget airline said after-tax profit for April to September fell 15% to €2.15 billion, as average fares dropped 4% and unhedged fuel prices doubled. It expects its fuel bill to rise by about €2 billion in the year to March 2028.
items.matters: Ryanair's chief executive, Michael O'Leary, expects European air fares to rise by 10% or more in 2027.

items.title: Oil prices fall about 3% on hopes for Qatar-mediated Iran talks
items.why: Brent crude fell about 3% to between $108 and $110 a barrel on Monday, and US crude to around $100, after three days of talks between Iranian and Qatari officials in Doha. Iran's foreign minister says the talks are progressing; President Trump has not ruled out resuming strikes.
items.matters: Oil prices feed into fuel, flight and food costs worldwide, and Brent ended October at a six-month high.

items.title: Juan Atkins, a founder of Detroit techno, dies aged 64
items.why: Juan Atkins, the American producer credited as a founding figure of techno, has died aged 64. He was found unresponsive in a hotel room in Mexico's capital, Mexico City, before a scheduled DJ set; his agency announced the death on 1 November. No cause has been given.
items.matters: His 1980s records as Cybotron and Model 500 helped give the genre, and its name, to dance floors worldwide.

items.title: Kimi Antonelli becomes Formula One's youngest world champion at 20
items.why: Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli clinched the 2026 Formula One title by finishing third at the Mexico City Grand Prix on 1 November, with four races left. Max Verstappen won the race ahead of Lewis Hamilton. Antonelli, 20, beats Sebastian Vettel's record as the youngest champion.
items.matters: He is the first Italian world champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

items.title: Sudan takes drone complaint against Ethiopia to UN and African Union
items.why: Sudan said late on Sunday it had complained to the UN Security Council and the African Union that the paramilitary RSF is launching drones from Ethiopian territory at civilian sites and power plants. Sudanese officials say hundreds of civilians have been killed or hurt. Ethiopia has previously denied the accusations.

items.title: Israeli election officials say results stand despite Likud fraud claims
items.why: The head of Israel's election committee, Justice Noam Sohlberg, said on Sunday the 27 October vote was conducted properly and the result will stand even if suspicions of foreign interference are confirmed. Netanyahu's Likud says, without evidence, that Arab-led parties 'stole' the election; Qatar denies involvement.
items.matters: Netanyahu's bloc won 53 of 120 seats, short of a majority; President Herzog begins coalition consultations on Wednesday.

items.changed: Updated: final count gives Iotova 57.6%, and Gyurov has accepted defeat.
items.title: Iliana Iotova wins Bulgaria's presidential runoff with 57.6% of the vote
items.why: Final results from Bulgaria's Central Election Commission give acting president Iliana Iotova 57.6% against 39.5% for the pro-Western former caretaker prime minister Andrey Gyurov, who has accepted defeat. She becomes Bulgaria's first elected woman president. Polling agencies put turnout below 30%.
items.matters: Iotova favours dialogue with Moscow and opposes military aid to Ukraine, while backing EU and NATO membership, AFP reports.

items.title: Sweden's Andreas Almgren and Kenya's Sheila Chepkirui win New York City Marathon
items.why: Andreas Almgren won the men's race in 2 hours 6 minutes 1 second on his marathon debut, 13 seconds ahead of Italy's Yemaneberhan Crippa. Sheila Chepkirui won the women's race in 2:24:36, six seconds ahead of the American Jess McClain.
items.matters: Almgren is the first Swedish runner to win one of the world's major marathons.

items.title: Bangladesh garment wage protests shut hundreds of factories for third day
items.why: Garment workers around Dhaka, Bangladesh's capital, protested for a third day on Monday, demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka ($242), up from 12,500. The manufacturers' association says 529 factories halted production on Sunday. The government has set up a wage board.
items.matters: Garments are Bangladesh's biggest export, and the unrest comes in the peak season for clothing orders.

items.title: Marc Marquez wins Malaysian MotoGP and can clinch the title in Qatar
items.why: Ducati's Marc Marquez won the Malaysian Grand Prix at Sepang on 1 November by about four seconds from Pedro Acosta, with his brother Alex third. It was his 80th premier-class win. He now leads the injured Jorge Martin by 44 points.
items.matters: He could seal an eighth MotoGP title at the Qatar Grand Prix next weekend.

items.title: Golden State Valkyries win the WNBA title in only their second season
items.why: The Valkyries beat the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in San Francisco on Saturday in the first Game 7 in WNBA Finals history. Gabby Williams scored 30 points, 28 of them in the second half, and was named Finals MVP.
items.matters: It is the first title for the expansion team, which joined the league in 2025.

items.title: Canelo Alvarez regains WBC super middleweight title in Riyadh
items.why: Mexico's Saul "Canelo" Alvarez beat Christian Mbilli by unanimous decision in Saudi Arabia's capital, Riyadh, on 31 October. The judges scored it 115-112, 116-111 and 117-110. It was Mbilli's first defence of the belt and his first professional defeat.

items.title: G20 foreign ministers end Atlanta meeting without agreement on key issues
items.why: The two-day meeting of G20 foreign ministers in Atlanta, in the US, ended on Saturday without a joint statement, mainly because of divisions over Russia's war in Ukraine, AP reports. The usual group photo was dropped after European and other ministers objected to posing with Russia's Sergey Lavrov.
items.matters: G20 leaders are due to meet in Florida in December; it is unclear whether Vladimir Putin will attend.

items.changed: Updated: Iran says the 'ball is in the US court'; Trump says the war will end soon 'one way or the other'.
items.title: Iran says 'ball is in US court' as Qatar-led talks continue
items.why: Iran's foreign ministry said on Monday the next move belongs to President Trump, after three days of indirect, Qatar-led talks without an apparent breakthrough. Trump says the war will end soon 'one way or the other'. Qatar says one of its gas tankers was hit in the Gulf on Friday.
items.matters: Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has ordered a 'geographically unrestricted response' to any new US or Israeli attack.

items.changed: Updated: the truce has ended and Kyiv says Russian attacks on the region have resumed.
items.title: Kherson truce ends after hundreds evacuated from occupied Oleshky
items.why: The six-day local ceasefire around Oleshky, in Ukraine's southern Kherson region, ended on Sunday evening after Russia turned down an extension, Ukrainian officials say. US First Lady Melania Trump, who helped broker it, says nearly 800 people left. Kyiv says Russian attacks on the region resumed on Monday.

items.title: Ebola deaths in the Democratic Republic of Congo pass 5,000
items.why: Congo's health ministry says the outbreak of the Bundibugyo strain, declared in May, has killed 5,026 people among 10,351 infections. Most cases are in the eastern provinces of Ituri and North Kivu. There is no approved vaccine or treatment for this strain.
items.matters: It is the second-deadliest Ebola outbreak on record; Kenya, Uganda and Nigeria have also reported cases.

items.title: Poland's president and government clash over control of constitutional court
items.why: Judges chosen by parliament entered Poland's Constitutional Tribunal in Warsaw on Friday and said they had suspended its chief justice. President Karol Nawrocki, who refuses to swear several of them in, confronted them inside and calls it a 'forceful takeover'. Donald Tusk's government says they were lawfully appointed.
items.matters: The European Commission says parliament has the right to appoint the judges; the dispute has run since 2015.

items.changed: Updated: withdrawals have restarted, with net outflows of $3.6 billion, and Binance says it has replaced 95% of the stolen tokens.
items.title: FBI blames North Korea for record $6.3 billion Binance crypto hack
items.why: The FBI says North Korean hackers it calls TraderTraitor stole more than $6 billion from Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, around 29 October. Withdrawals restarted on Sunday, with net outflows of $3.6 billion; Binance says it has replaced 95% of the stolen tokens.
